page: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton platform running on the custom ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the server provides 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with a single execution thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded execution and compilation efficiency. In Geekbench testing, the system achieved a multi-core score of 28306.0 and a clang compilation score of 91952.0, corroborated by 96125.19 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Data throughput is pronounced across compression workloads, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 36.47 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 623.71 GB/sec. In-memory data management and network workloads also deliver leading-class throughput, evidenced by 136.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 103.35 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Large-block memory transfers and standard encryption tests demonstrate average performance levels.

The primary operational tradeoff of this configuration lies in its architectural profile. While the dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores deliver high compute density per dollar without hyperthreading overhead, applications requiring x86 instruction sets or specialized vector extensions like AVX-512 cannot run without modification. Additionally, the lack of local NVMe storage requires all persistent and high-throughput scratch data to traverse the network fabric.

Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is engineered for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Key target applications include CI/CD build pipelines, distributed compilation clusters, containerized microservices, media transcoding, static web serving infrastructure, and in-memory key-value caching layers such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, featuring 48 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 cores clocked at 3.3 GHz and 96.0 GB of memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without simultaneous multithreading, it maintains a compute-centric 1:2 memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, paired with a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark measurements reflect top-tier throughput in parallel compute, Clang software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations exceeding 136 million operations per second. However, large uncached memory block transfers and cryptographic tests fall within median performance tiers. The instance delivers high resource density for scale-out parallel processing, making it well-matched for distributed software builds, continuous integration pipelines, static web serving clusters, and high-volume caching deployments.
